newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farm ministers call for more work on beef labels.
newsitem.headline: Farm ministers call for more work on beef labels.

text.p: EU farm ministers on Monday sent back proposals for cattle identification and beef labelling to the Special Committee on Agriculture, officials said.
"More technical discussions are needed. We hope to get an agreement early next year," Irish agriculture minister Ivan Yates told a news conference after a Farm Council.

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler, noting that during a preliminary discussion ministers supported the proposals in principle though not in detail, said he would urge the European Parliament to give its opinion quickly.
Several countries said they needed more time to introduce a computerised system for identifying animals and their movements and that the proposed January 1998 deadline was unrealistic.
Under the EU Commission proposal, member states would introduce ear tagging systems in January 1997.
On beef labelling, member states were split between those wanting voluntary schemes and those seeking compulsory measures.
Italy, Luxembourg, Britain, Netherlands, Denmark and Ireland were among those backing a voluntary scheme.
Most nations wanted only fresh beef to be labelled at first.
Fischler said he was against compulsory labelling because it would require stricter controls being carried out by member states and take longer to introduce.
"We want to make progress rapidly because everyone believes this would help revitalise the market," he said

The Netherlands, Belgium, Northern Ireland and Denmark, which have fairly advanced cattle identification systems, wanted to press ahead with the labelling scheme without waiting for all member states to comply.
